# OneLobby

> Open-source, game-agnostic multiplayer kit: lobby server with join codes, TURN relay, WebRTC data-channel clients for
> JavaScript, .NET, Godot 4 C# and Unity 6. Lockstep or raw messaging, host-authoritative state replication (.NET, JS, GDScript), voice
> and text chat, self-hostable, games stay playable offline.

## Start here

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): what OneLobby is, the API on one screen for C# and JS, and the rules
- [examples/tictactoe/README.md](examples/tictactoe/README.md): a single-player browser game to practise on

Lobby events (JS `lobby.on(name)`; C# has PascalCase events for most, e.g. `PeerReady`, `MessageReceived`): peerJoined, peerReady (data link to that peer open; reliable
sends made before it are queued and flushed, not dropped), ready and the `lobby.ready` promise (C# `Ready`, `ReadyAsync`:
a joiner's link to the host is open; the host is ready at once), peerLeft, joinRequested, hostChanged, phase,
message, metaChanged, serverLost, sessionEnded.

JS defaults: host() is unlisted unless visibility "public"; empty displayName shows as "Player N"; a joiner that cannot
reach the host in readyTimeoutMs (15000) fails with code ice_failed (sessionEnded reason "ice_failed"); rememberSeat keeps
the seat across a reload (kit.resume(), kit.rememberedCode); seams go under options.advanced; describeError(e),
shareUrl(code) and codeFromUrl() are player-facing helpers. C#: OneLobbyConfig.ReadyTimeout (15 s, Zero = forever)
does the same as readyTimeoutMs (ReadyAsync faults with OneLobbyException code ice_failed); Unity's OneLobbyRunner keeps
Application.runInBackground on while in a lobby (KeepRunningInBackground); ReplicationSession.Clients counts a peer only
once its link is up (ClientReady). Install: npm install onelobby, or the script-tag
build dist/onelobby.global.min.js (window.OneLobby).

## Recipes

- [Blueprint flow](.claude/skills/onelobby/SKILL.md): survey a game, get a recommendation (`create-onelobby --recommend --json`), write onelobby.json (schema [spec/blueprint.schema.json](spec/blueprint.schema.json), design [docs/design/blueprint.md](docs/design/blueprint.md)), build with the scaffolder and the drop-in menu, `create-onelobby verify`
- [Telling the player why](docs/recipes/diagnostics.md): a plain cause and next step on every connect failure (`err.diagnosis`, `describeError`), the host's `peerDiagnosis` line, `kit.netLog` (Copy logs, masked), `kit.checkConnection()`; spec/diagnostics.md; nothing is sent anywhere but to the host the player dialed (JS, C# and GDScript; `Diagnosis` / `peer_diagnosis` / `NetLog` / `CheckConnectionAsync` / `check_connection`)
- [Room layer](docs/recipes/room.md): names, per-player data, ready, countdown, spectators, kick and ban with reasons, passwords (JS, C# and GDScript)
- [Godot 4 C#](docs/recipes/godot-csharp.md): add the menu scene (`OneLobbyMenu.tscn`) to a Godot project, or build your own Host / Join / Browse buttons; `npx create-onelobby my-game --template godot-csharp --yes` (or `--into <project>`) sets it up: NuGet references, pinned menu, WebRTC natives, direct hosting, headless two-peer test; `verify` proves it on 127.0.0.1, `update` moves the menu and the package versions
- [Godot 4 GDScript](docs/recipes/godot-gdscript.md): the same in GDScript, no .NET (raw and lockstep, chat, pause, room layer); `npx create-onelobby my-game --template godot-gdscript --yes` (or `--into <project>`) sets it all up: add-on, WebRTC natives, autoload, menu, headless two-peer test; `npx create-onelobby verify` proves it on 127.0.0.1 (`VERIFY_OK`), `update` re-vendors the add-on
- [Drop-in menu](docs/recipes/menu.md): the Godot scene, the Unity `OneLobbyMenu` component (one `AddComponent`, no prefab) and the web `<one-lobby>` element draw the same screens (see its "Web" section for attributes, events, parts and rewording).
- [Godot drop-in menu](docs/recipes/menu.md): one scene (`menu.tscn`) with name, host, join, lobby roster, ready, kick and ban, relay field, connection check and plain-words errors; `game_started` is the whole integration (GDScript); the same scene for Godot C# (`addons/onelobby_menu/OneLobbyMenu.tscn`, `GameStarted`) over the engine-free `MenuModel` in `OneLobby.Core`
- [Unity 6](docs/recipes/unity.md): the com.onelobby.unity package (UnityTransport over OneLobby.DataChannel/libdatachannel, OneLobbyRunner, voice); desktop now, no WebGL
- [Browser JS](docs/recipes/js-web.md): the same in a plain web page
- [Generic .NET](docs/recipes/dotnet-generic.md): console or any engine; DataChannelTransport (libdatachannel WebRTC) for real play, the in-memory transport for tests
- [Which setup fits](clients/js/packages/create-onelobby/README.md): `npx create-onelobby --recommend "<one line about the game>" [--json]` proposes sync mode, tick rate, players, pause and hosting with a reason per choice (deterministic, no network; five shapes)
- [Raw mode](docs/recipes/raw-mode.md): bring your own netcode (host-authoritative, turn-based)
- [Replicated state](docs/recipes/replication.md): OneLobby.Replication (C#), ReplicationSession (JS) and OneLobbyReplicationSession (GDScript) on raw mode: delta snapshots, interpolation, inputs, events, prediction, lag-compensated hitscan
- [Voice and chat](docs/recipes/voice-and-chat.md): push-to-talk, mute, text chat
- [Shared pause](docs/recipes/pause.md): anyone pauses for everyone, the pauser or host resumes; host policy hook, Clear before a restart; lockstep frames stop while paused
- [Headless testing](docs/recipes/testing.md): two browser contexts with playwright-core, fake mic
- [Host with a join code](docs/recipes/direct-ip.md): no server at all; the host's .NET game or Node server runs the hub, opens port 47810 TCP+UDP on the router (UPnP/NAT-PMP) and shows a join code that is its address; joiners in C#, Node or a browser paste it
- [Browser game hosted from Node](docs/recipes/browser-game.md): the host's Node game server is a direct host that serves the game page on port 47810; friends open one link, the page joins the address it came from through a WebSocket-shaped adapter (heartbeat, rate limit, fallback when WebRTC is missing)
- [Game console (ogc1)](docs/recipes/game-console.md): a loopback-only, token-authenticated HTTP door so a local tool or agent can send dev commands to a running game; off by default
- [Saved player settings](docs/recipes/settings.md): name, relay line (masked), last code and lobby server saved on the player's machine and applied as defaults (`kit.settings`, `client.Settings`, `client.settings`), `ONELOBBY_NAME` / `ONELOBBY_RELAY` / `ONELOBBY_LAST_CODE` / `ONELOBBY_LOBBY_SERVER` override, never logged; spec/settings.md
- [TURN relay for Direct mode](docs/recipes/turn.md): bring-your-own TURN for strict NATs (coturn or hosted), per-client config, expiring logins, troubleshooting
- [Self-host](docs/recipes/self-host.md): run the lobby server and relay yourself (hosted backend, later)

## API reference (generated by docs/build.mjs)

- [.NET client](docs/api/dotnet.md): every public type of OneLobby.Core, OneLobby.Godot and OneLobby.Replication
